questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you need to identify all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt for damage or wear. If any parts are not belt-driven, tell the examiner. Make sure all parts work properly, are mounted securely, and have no damage or leaks.

questions.question: How many seconds before a bus stop should warning lights turn on?
questions.explanation: School buses with amber warning lights must turn them on at least 200 feet before the stop. This equals about five to ten seconds of driving time.

questions.question: When boarding a school bus, students should:
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly and in a single-file line. For safety, they must use the handrail when boarding.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, you should not:

options.text: Make sure the steering box is firmly attached.
Check for leaks in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Check for power steering fluid leaks and damage to hoses.

questions.question: If students cause trouble on the bus while others are getting off, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the back of the bus immediately to stop the problem while students leave.
Wait until all students have left, then handle the problem.
Have another student handle it while you watch students exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until all students have left, then handle the problem.
questions.explanation: Loading and unloading students needs your full attention. If behavior problems happen during this time, wait until all students are safely off the bus before you address the issue.

questions.question: What can outside crossover mirrors show the driver?

options.text: The right side of the bus
The left side of the bus

questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help the driver see dangerous areas directly in front of the bus and to the left and right sides, from the front bumper to the service door.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to check all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt if the vehicle has them.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing in a placarded vehicle, you should always:

options.text: Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while crossing the tracks.
Change lanes while crossing the tracks.

questions.explanation: Before crossing railroad tracks in a placarded vehicle, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: In a basic vehicle control skills test, a look means:

options.text: Checking the gauges on the dashboard.
Getting out of your seat and walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Getting out of your seat and walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look happens when you open your door, leave your seat, and walk to the back to check where the vehicle is. For straight line backing, you can only do one look. For other exercises, you can do up to two looks.

questions.question: Properly adjusted outside convex mirrors should let the driver see:

options.text: The full side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
The rear door of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
questions.explanation: Outside convex mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see at least one traffic lane on each side of the bus, the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: A school bus stop:

options.text: Can be added by the driver if students are told about the change.
Should be voted on by students and parents.
Should be set by the school and stay the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be set by the school and stay the same.
questions.explanation: A bus driver should never change or add a stop without written approval from the school district.

questions.question: Before a trip, make sure that:

options.text: The grooved pedal surface is not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved pedal surface is not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip check, make sure nothing blocks the pedals. Check that pedals work properly and have their grooved surface intact.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, you will need to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the power steering fluid is above the full mark.
Make sure the power steering fluid is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the dipstick is and confirm there is enough fluid. The fluid level must be above the refill mark, not above the full mark.

questions.question: When entering traffic on an expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.explanation: When entering an expressway, check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: Student safety is best kept by:

options.text: Letting some students leave while others stay on.
Letting all students leave the bus.

questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safer and easier to control if they stay on the bus.

questions.question: If a school bus must be evacuated, passengers should:
questions.explanation: During an emergency evacuation, the driver must decide which exit or exits are safest and tell students to use those exits.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without an accident.
Show you can use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show you can use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the test, drive safely and responsibly. Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and complete the test without accidents or violations.

questions.question: Adjust a bus's mirrors:

options.text: At the first stoplight after your shift starts.

questions.explanation: Check and adjust mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: If your bus has a roof-mounted strobe light, use it:
questions.explanation: Use the roof-mounted strobe light when visibility is poor.

questions.question: What should properly adjusted outside side flat mirrors let the driver see?

options.text: The sides of the school bus
The front tires on the ground
Vehicles in front of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides of the school bus
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted outside side flat mirrors let the driver see along the bus sides, the rear tires on the ground, and 200 feet behind the bus.
